# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 4, 2026
4 12:51a ○ cleanDoubleSlashes lacks respectQueryAndFragment option that trailing-slash helpers already have
5 " ○ cleanDoubleSlashes collapses slashes in the whole string by splitting only on "://"
6 " ◆ cleanDoubleSlashes gains opt-in respectQueryAndFragment flag
S3 Add an opt-in `respectQueryAndFragment` flag to `cleanDoubleSlashes` so `//` inside the query string and fragment is preserved, with the default behaviour unchanged and tests added. (Nov 4, 12:51 AM)
**Investigated**: Searched `src`, `test`, and `README.md` for `cleanDoubleSlashes` and `respectQueryAndFragment`. Read the trailing-slash helpers (`hasTrailingSlash`, `withoutTrailingSlash`, `withTrailingSlash`) in `src/utils.ts`, which already accept the flag. Read the existing `cleanDoubleSlashes` implementation, its README entry, its JSDoc, and `test/double-slash.test.ts`. Checked `parsePath` in `src/parse.ts`.

**Learned**: `cleanDoubleSlashes` splits on `://`, collapses `/{2,}` in each segment, and rejoins, so it has no notion of query or fragment. The trailing-slash helpers use `#` and `?` splitting when the flag is set and plain string operations otherwise. The existing tests covered only path and scheme cases.

**Completed**: `cleanDoubleSlashes(input, respectQueryAndFragment?)` in `src/utils.ts` now finds the first `?` or `#`, cleans only the prefix, and keeps the suffix when the flag is `true`. Without the flag, the original logic runs. The JSDoc gained a description and example. The README entry was renamed to the new signature with a new example. `test/double-slash.test.ts` gained a `respectQueryAndFragment` block with six table cases and a default-behaviour test. Prettier was run on the changed files. `test/double-slash.test.ts` passes 12 of 12 tests, and `tsc --noEmit` reported no errors. Nothing has been committed. The full test suite has not been run.

**Next Steps**: The session is ongoing. The next likely step is to run the full test suite to check for regressions beyond the double-slash tests. Any further requests from the user have not yet been seen.

**Notes**: The flag name matches the trailing-slash helpers, so the API is consistent across the utils. The default path is untouched, so existing callers are unaffected. Only the targeted test file has been run, so broader coverage is still unconfirmed.
